verdict: OK to lend in Warangal ginning and pressing, but only to empanelled modern factories with clean stock-and-book discipline; avoid traders running single-season gins on borrowed working capital.
title: Warangal cotton ginning & pressing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
**Cash is made on the spread between kapas purchase price and lint sale price, not on volume alone.** The cycle is brutally seasonal: heavy kapas buying in a few weeks, bales sold over months, so working capital peaks fast and the bank funds the peak. **Ginning adds little value, so the margin is thin and the game is speed and recovery, not price.** [9][11]

## What has changed now
Warangal is running a formal empanelment of modern ginning and pressing factories for cotton season 2026-27, with EMD of Rs 50,000 and a 365-day empanelment period [1]. **That is a filter you can use: empanelled, modern-press units are the ones with a reason to keep quality and records straight.** CCI is also tendering in Telangana [2], which tells you government procurement is active in the belt. Telangana GST collections are up 13.8% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand up 15.7% against 9.5% [D] — the local economy is moving faster than the national one. **So when a proposal lands, check the empanelment certificate and the press type first; if the unit is not empanelled, ask why and price for it.**

## Where the growth is
Peer results show the split clearly. AB Cotspin's Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52.94% to Rs 102.01 crore but operating margin fell to 12.90% from 22.29% [4][5] — volume without spread. Sportking nearly doubled EBITDA margin to 19.8% in Q2 FY27 from 10.4% [7], and Nitin Spinners is adding Rs 200-300 crore of incremental revenue in FY2027 [6]. **Pursue ginners who sell to such mills on contract and who own their press; avoid pure kapas traders who gin on job work.** Rating reports stress that proximity to cotton-growing areas cuts logistics cost [10] and that vertically integrated ginners with captive ginning and power do better [8]. **Warangal sits in the belt, so favour units within the growing area with their own press and some seed-oil linkage.**

## How to grow safely
Structure as a cash-credit or CC limit against hypothecation of stock and book debts, with a separate season limit that steps down after the buying peak. **Take stock-and-book statements every month, and bale-wise sale register every fortnight during the season.** Covenant on drawing power computed on paid stock, not on godown value. **If the unit cannot show the sale register, ask for the mill-wise ledger and the GST returns together.** [D] gives you the macro tailwind; the discipline has to come from the file. ## Early warning signs
- Monthly stock statement (monthly): stock ageing beyond one season -> stop fresh kapas limits and inspect godown. - Bale sale register (fortnightly): lint sold below the season's average recovery price -> ask for mill contract copies and reprice the limit. - GST returns vs sales (monthly): turnover mismatch -> freeze enhancement and seek reconciliation. - Empanelment status (annual): lapse or non-renewal for the season -> treat as a downgrade trigger. [1]

Sources say little specific about Warangal city itself beyond the empanelment tender [1]; the rest is first principles plus peers. Some rating reports cited are old — S.S. Cotton is a 2017 rating [9] — so use them for structure, not for current numbers.
